jobs.title: Executive Director
jobs.description:
The Wisconsin FFA Foundation, Inc., is seeking a dynamic and forward-thinking Executive Director to lead our organization into its next era of impact and growth.

The Foundation supports over 28,000 FFA members across the state through partnership with the Wisconsin Association of FFA, the Wisconsin FFA Center, the Wisconsin Association of Agricultural Educators, and the Wisconsin FFA Alumni & Supporters.

The Executive Director provides strategic and operational leadership for the Foundation, advancing its vision to expand access to agricultural education and FFA for students across Wisconsin.

The Executive Director leads the Foundation’s fundraising and development efforts, builds and stewards relationships with donors, corporate partners and other stakeholders, oversees Foundation operations and staff, and works closely with the Board of Directors to achieve the organization’s strategic and financial goals.

The Executive Director partners with the Board in developing and implementing strategic plans and annual budgets while having the day-to-day autonomy to make decisions and lead the organization within established priorities and policies.   The Executive Director also serves as a key ambassador for the Foundation and its mission.

Job Responsibilities
:
Fundraising & Revenue Development: Provide strategic leadership for fundraising (corporate and individual giving, grants, endowment growth, and Foundation fundraisers) in partnership with the Development Officer, personally engaging major donors to help close key gifts and working to meet annual revenue goals.

Grants, Scholarships & Fund Disbursement: Oversee the full cycle of the Foundation's giving, including grants, scholarships, and other disbursements.

Financial Management: Manage the Foundation's budget, cash flow, bill payment, audits, and tax filings, providing the Board with regular financial reporting.

Relationship & Partnership Management: Build and steward relationships with Team Ag Ed partners, business and industry, donors, and the general public.

Staff Leadership: Lead and support a three-person staff team, delegating clearly to build a collaborative, high-functioning operation.

Board Relations & Governance: Serve as the primary liaison between the Board and staff, keeping the Board informed and ensuring its directives are carried out effectively.

Nonprofit Governance & Compliance: Maintain the Foundation's 501(c)(3) status and ensure compliance with all applicable legal and regulatory requirements.

Required Qualifications
:
A bachelor’s degree in agriculture, business, communications, or a closely related field, or
equivalent professional experience.
5+ years of leadership experience in nonprofit or business management, program oversight, financial management, and/or stakeholder relations.
Experience in fundraising, development, donor relations,  sales, marketing, business development, or another relationship-driven revenue function.
Ability to travel up to 25% of the time (same-day) with occasional overnight travel.
Highly organized with strong project management skills.
Excellent written and verbal communication skills.
Must possess a valid driver’s license and proof of current motor vehicle insurance.
Must have a passion for agriculture and youth development.

Preferred Qualifications
:
Experience supervising direct reports, including remote supervision.
Demonstrated experience working collaboratively with a governing board and volunteer leaders.
Operational experience spanning human resources, finance, technology, and administration.
Experience with endowed gifts, corporate partnerships, sponsorships, grants or other development programs.
Strong relationship-building skills with donors, partners, stakeholders, and volunteers.

Compensation
: $75,000 – $100,000 base salary, commensurate with experience. Salary and compensation reviewed annually based on performance evaluation.

Benefits
: Cell phone reimbursement, simple IRA match, holiday pay, managed time off, Health Reimbursement Account

Employment is contingent on the completion of a background check.

If interested in this position, please email a cover letter and resume to Kelly Wilfert, Wisconsin FFA Foundation Board President at kellytwilfert@gmail.com. Please include “Executive Director Application – [Your Name]” in the subject line. For more information or questions, please email Kelly or call 920-323-7865.

The Wisconsin FFA Foundation, Inc. is an equal opportunity employer and any information collected is solely to verify identity and determine suitability for the position.

jobs.title: Fractional Director of Development and Strategic Partnerships
jobs.description:
Position Type:
Part-Time (15–20 hours/week)
Location:
Remote 
Reports to:
President

About KrabbeConnect

KrabbeConnect is a nonprofit dedicated to improving the lives of individuals and families affected by Krabbe disease through education, advocacy, family support, and research. We are committed to bridging the gap between science and the patient community while working toward better treatments and ultimately a cure.

Position Summary

KrabbeConnect is seeking a motivated, relationship-driven Director of Development and Strategic Partnerships
to expand our network within the rare disease and biotechnology communities while growing philanthropic support for our mission. This individual will focus on identifying new funding opportunities, cultivating corporate and foundation partnerships, and strengthening relationships that lead to sustainable fundraising. The ideal candidate is an excellent communicator who enjoys networking, building meaningful partnerships, and turning connections into long-term supporters.

Key Responsibilities

Strategic Partnerships

• Build and maintain relationships with pharmaceutical, biotechnology, healthcare, and other corporate partners aligned with KrabbeConnect’s mission
• Develop relationships with organizations across rare/genetic disease, newborn screening, and patient advocacy communities to expand collaboration, visibility, and shared impact
• Cultivate relationships with community foundations, family foundations, philanthropic organizations, and high-capacity individuals who have the potential to become long-term supporters of KrabbeConnect
• Represent KrabbeConnect at conferences, community events, networking opportunities, and virtual meetings to expand the organization’s network and identify prospective partners and supporters
• Steward existing corporate, foundation, community, and major-donor relationships through meaningful engagement, regular communication, and demonstrated impact

Fundraising & Development

• Develop and manage a pipeline of prospective corporate sponsors, foundations, major donors, and other funding opportunities, with clear strategies for moving prospects from identification to solicitation and ongoing support
• Create compelling sponsorship proposals, grant requests, major-gift opportunities, and customized partnership packages aligned with organizational and donor priorities
• Identify and pursue opportunities for corporate sponsorships, foundation funding, major gifts, cause-marketing campaigns, and other philanthropic support
• Secure funding to support KrabbeConnect’s programs, research initiatives, family assistance, education, awareness efforts, and organizational priorities
• Lead and support fundraising campaigns and events, including Putt-Putt to #curekrabbe, Anywhere Strides, Giving Tuesday, Year-End Giving Campaign, and other development initiatives
• Work with our CRM consultant to maintain accurate donor, prospect, solicitation, and partnership activity within the organization’s CRM to support follow-up, relationship management, reporting, and revenue forecasting
• Track fundraising progress and evaluate results to identify opportunities for increased donor engagement, retention, and revenue growth

Grant & Foundation Research

• Identify grant opportunities aligned with KrabbeConnect's mission
• Assist with gathering information and coordinating grant submissions
• Maintain a calendar of funding deadlines and reporting requirements

Relationship Management

• Serve as a primary point of contact for prospective partners
• Steward existing corporate and foundation relationships
• Coordinate follow-up communications and partnership recognition

Collaboration

• Work closely with board members to leverage existing relationships
• Support the development of fundraising materials, sponsorship packets, and donor communications
• Provide regular updates on fundraising pipeline, partnership development, and progress toward revenue goals

Preferred Qualifications

• Bachelor’s degree in nonprofit management, business, communications, public administration, or a related field; advanced degree or CFRE certification is beneficial
• Demonstrated experience in fundraising, including Annual Giving and Planned Giving programs, with a strong understanding of Philanthropy
• Proficiency in Budgeting and financial oversight related to development activities, including forecasting and revenue tracking
• Ability to build and manage strategic partnerships with individual donors, foundations, corporations, and community organizations
• Strong communication, presentation, and relationship-building skills, with the ability to engage diverse stakeholders and convey complex information clearly
• Experience in nonprofit development, preferably within healthcare, rare disease, or patient advocacy environments
• Proven skills in donor stewardship, grant writing, and development of fundraising materials and campaigns
• The ability to travel by car or plane when necessary
• Experience using donor management or CRM systems is a plus
• Passion for rare disease advocacy and improving patient outcomes

Compensation

• Part-time, flexible schedule (15–20 hours per week)
• Compensation will be commensurate with experience and formal education
• Opportunity for performance-based bonus tied to fundraising goals

KrabbeConnect is an equal opportunity employer. We are committed to building a team that reflects diverse experiences, perspectives, and backgrounds. We welcome qualified applicants regardless of race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, age, disability, veteran status, or any other characteristic protected by law.
